speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and the recalled ant bite, this lesion is highly suspicious for Cutaneous Leishmaniasis or a deep fungal infection like Blastomycosis. Given your immunocompromised status from steroid use for uveitis, we must rule out atypical mycobacteria or nocardiosis as well. Can you tell me if the edges of the ulcer are raised and rolled, or if the base appears to have a "punched-out" look? Do you notice any satellite lesions nearby? REQUEST IMAGES: Leg_Ulcer_Close_Up.
